leaned_rules.tmux_dedup_protocol: Rule 18 (TMUX-DEDUP -- S112 operator-confirmed root cause + standing fix; encoded via the governed add-rule verb, NOT a hand-edit; SUPERSEDES the one-time TMUX-DEDUP-INSTANCE "restart/reconnect the connector" framing). ROOT CAUSE (E-048): Claude Desktop does NOT reap its tmux-mcp MCP child process on exit, so every relaunch spawns a NEW tmux-mcp instance beside the stale one. Two (or more) "npm exec tmux-mcp" instances then race over the socket /tmp/tmux-1000/default; only one owns/creates the tmux server, so any tmux-mcp call routed to the other instance hits a dead server ("no server running on /tmp/tmux-1000/default"). This is a recurring per-relaunch artifact, NOT a Cowork connector mis-registration -- there is no operator config to change and no operator action required. STANDING FIX (apply at session start, or on the first tmux "no server"/race symptom): (1) pgrep -af tmux-mcp -- if more than one "npm exec tmux-mcp" process tree exists, duplication is present. (2) ps -o pid,ppid,etimes,lstart,cmd -p <pids> -- the OLDER tree (larger etimes / earlier lstart) is the stale leftover from the previous Desktop exit; the NEWEST tree is the live one the current MCP connection routes to. (3) kill the OLDER full tree ONLY (kill the node + sh + npm PIDs of that tree); NEVER kill the newest/active tree. (4) verify exactly one instance remains (pgrep) and tmux-mcp responds (list-sessions). EDGE CASE: if tmux-mcp reports "no server" with a SINGLE instance present, that is merely an empty server with no sessions -- create one (wsl-exec: tmux new-session -d -s main, or tmux-mcp create-session) rather than killing anything. wsl-exec is the reliable ATOMIC fallback transport throughout (it ran 100% clean while tmux raced; mind its operator-stripping gotchas in known_issues_registry). Established S112: the immediate duplicate (older tree) was killed, one live instance confirmed, and this procedure baked in so no future session re-diagnoses E-048.

known_issues_registry.sandbox_mount_truncation: CRITICAL (S22+S23). SANDBOX IS PERMANENTLY BANNED. S22 burned ~30% context on truncation. S23 burned ~30% context on stale .pyc (E-031). RULE: NEVER use sandbox for ANY purpose in this project. wsl-exec with working_dir is the ONLY permitted test/shell runner. pytest is installed at /home/pakhol/.local/bin/pytest (S23). If wsl-exec fails: ASK USER. Do NOT fall back to sandbox.
known_issues_registry.wsl_exec_subshell: CRITICAL. wsl-exec strips backticks, $(), and pipe | characters. NEVER pass subshell expansion inline. Use temp bash script for commands requiring subshell operators (e.g., git push with $(cat PAT)). Violations caused credential leaks E-011, E-032.

Establish ground truth BEFORE acting. Do NOT panic-switch environments on first failure. known_issues_registry.curl_cffi_headers: curl_cffi: NEVER pass custom headers= when using impersonate=. Custom headers override the impersonated TLS/header fingerprint and break the bypass. Discovered in eBay S1 — get_headers() function broke curl_cffi impersonation, re-triggering 403.

leaned_rules.report_before_transfer: Rule 12 (S45 origin; RE-SETTLED S47 per user-approved Task 5/6 — full revision + R/A/G thresholds). RAG is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH so this rule lives HERE. BLOCKING GATE: on EVERY substantial completion (milestone shipped, commit+checkpoint done, end of a unit of work) the assistant MUST AUTOMATICALLY RENDER THE FULL STATUS REPORT IN CHAT as the response itself — NEVER written to disk, NEVER a file or present_files card (a report file pollutes root_project; cf. the reconciliation-audit reprimand). DESIGN PRINCIPLE (S47): the report is a DETERMINISTIC RENDER of the RAG canonical fields, not hand-authored prose — it RENDERS state, never re-proses or re-authors operating_protocol/backlog text (DRY; pre-aligns with DRIFT-ELIM where docs are renders never authorities). Dashboard-first / inverted-pyramid: verdict and health at the top. Borrows ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 (assessment+control: planned-vs-actual + corrective action), 15289 (report identification metadata) and PM highlight-report practice (R/A/G + objective thresholds + Road-to-Green); borrows their INTENT but NOT their ~10-20pp length — a chat-rendered, LLM-re-ingested report must stay compact to protect the context budget (the no-compaction hard rule). CANONICAL FORMAT = 7 sections; heading '## RAG Runtime Kernel — Status Report (S<NN> close)', then: (1) AT-A-GLANCE markdown table | Overall | Milestone | Release-ready | Tests/Health | Drift gate | Context% | RAG seq | with R/A/G glyphs, immediately followed by '**Verdict:**' one honest line (say UNRELEASED/not-deployable when true, per Rule 14 increment-status-honesty); (2) BUILD planned-vs-actual table | # | Increment | Plan | Status | RAG | Commit·S | covering every increment + the release row; (3) THIS SESSION — what changed, <=5 bullets, no prose wall; (4) BACKLOG rendered from the RAG (Open / Blocked-or-user-gated / Deferred), IDs + one line each, never re-prosed; (5) RISKS & DEVIATIONS (Road-to-Green) — ONLY Amber/Red items: risk -> impact -> corrective action; (6) LEDGER & ERRORS — N OPEN + open E-### one-liners; (7) VERIFICATION & HANDOFF — latest commit, tests, health, drift-gate sha, RAG seq + written_by + bytes + .bak, next/handoff. R/A/G THRESHOLDS (objective, not subjective): RED = failing tests OR health < full OR drift-gate red OR a published repo-claim contradicts reality (Rule 11) OR context forced compaction; AMBER = feature-complete but UNRELEASED/not-deployable, OR an open user-gated blocker, OR within tolerance but trending; GREEN = released AND tests/health/drift all green AND repo-claims reconciled. Recurring operational gotchas are REFERENCE (they live in operating_protocol) — include them in the report ONLY if something changed this session, else omit. TRIGGERS (S47 user-clarified): (a) AUTOMATIC on completion of a significant task OR batch of tasks / milestone-commit — any commit-worthy/checkpoint-worthy unit — AND, CRITICALLY, PROACTIVELY whenever context is approaching a level that could provoke Cowork compaction/compression or ANY context-loss procedure: the report render + RAG checkpoint IS the state-preservation act and MUST happen BEFORE any such loss can occur (works in concert with context_window_management's ~70% halt + session_scope_discipline — never wait until compaction is imminent; render+checkpoint early enough that zero state is at risk). Calibrate firing to context risk, not to every trivial task — do not over-fire on micro-edits when no context pressure / transfer / request exists. (b) AUTOMATIC before ANY advisal/mention/recommendation to transfer to a new session (report first, transfer second). (c) ON-DEMAND at ANY time the user asks, phrased any way — ANY message SEMANTICALLY perceived as a call for the canonical/full 'Status Report' settled here MUST render THIS exact format regardless of wording. REPORT-INTENT CLASSIFICATION (S47 dual-POV design — canonical-report call vs ANY other interim report): intent recognition with ONE designated POSITIVE class. POSITIVE (=canonical) signals: the request's semantic target is the OVERALL PROJECT DEV-STATUS — 'status', 'where are we', 'the report', 'full report', 'rundown', 'state of the project', progress/health/release-readiness/tests/RAG-state, or a session-close/pre-transfer context. NEGATIVE (=some OTHER report) signals: the request is SCOPED to a narrower/different subject/artifact — e.g. 'report on the eBay deliverables', 'a comparison/benchmark report', 'summarize this file', 'an error report for E-040', 'a research report on vector DBs'. DECISION RULE: classify CANONICAL iff target is overall dev-status AND NOT scoped to a different artifact; a scope qualifier naming another subject flips it to OTHER; the bare unqualified word 'report' in a project-dev context DEFAULTS to canonical (it is the project's primary report). AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION (S47 — replaces 'just ask' with DECLARE-AND-PROCEED): because rendering the canonical report is CHEAP, SAFE and REVERSIBLE, do NOT block on a clarifying question by default. When intent cannot be recognized strictly/distinctly, render the MOST-LIKELY report (defaulting to canonical whenever a dev-status reading is plausible) PREFIXED with ONE explicit declared-assumption line naming which report you are producing and how to redirect (e.g. 'Reading this as the canonical Status Report — say so if you meant a different report'). This keeps momentum (no round-trip) while making the interpretation OBSERVABLE and one-line-CORRECTABLE — same fail-loud/cheap-error philosophy as the DRIFT-ELIM auditor. RESERVE a true blocking AskUserQuestion ONLY when (i) the subject itself is unidentifiable, OR (ii) the candidate interpretations diverge EXPENSIVELY (a costly/irreversible action hangs on the guess). POV tension resolved: AI/ML lens wants flexible semantic matching, CS lens wants deterministic fail-safe low-cost-error handling; convergence = explicit signal lists + a safe canonical DEFAULT + a declared, correctable assumption (LLM proposes intent; declared-default-plus-cheap-correction decides; render+checkpoint persists state). SCOPE GUARD: this canonical format governs ONLY the project-DEV-STATUS report; OTHER project reports unrelated to dev status are legitimately articulated/formatted differently — do NOT force them into this template. ENFORCEMENT: the assistant may NOT offer, mention, or recommend a session transfer unless this full report is already rendered IN THE SAME MESSAGE, ABOVE the transfer suggestion — report first, transfer second; the user must NEVER have to ask. WHY: promised pre-S45 but mis-stored in Cowork memory and violated in S45 (E-039); moved into operating_protocol so it loads as authoritative state every session start; re-settled S47 to fix the redundancy/readability gaps (3-4x duplicated facts, buried verdict, binary status) found in the S46 specimen.
leaned_rules.token_economy: Rule 17 (TOKEN-ECONOMY / CONTEXT-EMISSION DISCIPLINE — KA-15, S108; source: eBay Session-Zero field incident, triaged UNIVERSAL per deployment_test_result_triage / Rule 15). A three-in-one backpressure rule that guards the no-compaction hard rule (context_window_management) and the one-milestone discipline (session_scope_discipline). (1) BOUNDED TOOL-OUTPUT: NEVER capture whole panes or unbounded command/log/test output into the context window — a single oversized emission can spike the token budget and provoke the forbidden Cowork compaction. Pipe verbose output to a file and read back ONLY a bounded slice — e.g. `cmd >/tmp/out.txt 2>&1; tail -n 40 /tmp/out.txt` (or grep/head/wc -l) — cap dumps, prefer counts and heads over full bodies, and request the smallest emission that answers the question. (2) MALFORMED-EMISSION IS A FIRST-CLASS CIRCUIT_BREAKER STRIKE: a garbled, truncated, or malformed tool emission is a STRIKE under the Two-Strike Rule (circuit_breaker / Rule 5), not noise to retry blindly. On the second malformed or non-advancing emission toward one goal, HALT, diagnose root cause, log to ERROR_LOG.md, and switch to the cheapest bounded fallback — re-firing the same unbounded call is a NEW failure, not a new attempt. (3) KNOWN-ISSUE malformed_emission: under context bloat a harness can emit malformed/garbled tool output (observed eBay S0, where harness mangling compounded with the agent never loading HOT rule bodies into cognition and a non-atomic close that stranded the operator); treat any malformed emission as a fail-loud signal. WHY: established S108 (KA-15) from the eBay Session-Zero audit where context-bloat + whole-pane captures + malformed harness emission compounded into a stranded session; this is the universal backpressure so it cannot recur on any deployment. SPEC-SEED follow-up (TRACKED, DEFERRED): INIT-spec seeding — §15 token_economy bounded-output clause, §21 circuit-breaker malformed-emission strike, and the §41 known_issues_registry malformed_emission entry (universal; both the human-readable table and the rag-config block) — is bundled into the KA-14..17 arc release, sibling to the KA-13 / KA-14 spec-wiring follow-ups; until that release lands this live-RAG rule is authoritative for this deployment.
leaned_rules.inference_ledger_protocol: Rule 10 — INFERENCE CAPTURE. (1) TRIGGER: When reasoning yields a solution, idea, design decision, optimization, or follow-up that is NOT being implemented in the current session, it MUST be appended to inference_ledger IMMEDIATELY — not at session close, not retroactively. The trigger is involuntary: if you verbalize it, you log it. (2) ENTRY FORMAT: {id, session, type, summary, context, disposition, scheduled_as, superseded_by}. Types: solution | idea | design_decision | optimization | follow_up. Dispositions: OPEN → SCHEDULED | DEFERRED | SUPERSEDED | DISCARDED. (3) REVIEW: At session close, scan all OPEN items. Each MUST get a disposition with a one-line reason. SCHEDULED items get moved to open_tasks with a concrete ID. DEFERRED items stay in ledger with a reason. SUPERSEDED items link to what replaced them. DISCARDED items get a reason. (4) SESSION START: After loading RAG, scan ledger for OPEN items. Report count to user. If any OPEN items are stale (>2 sessions old without review), flag as overdue. (5) RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER STORES: inference_ledger is the INTAKE buffer. open_tasks is the COMMITTED backlog. deferred_items is the PARKED backlog. The ledger feeds both — items flow from ledger to tasks/deferred via SCHEDULED/DEFERRED disposition. Nothing enters open_tasks or deferred_items without first passing through the ledger (except user-directed additions). (6) WHY THIS EXISTS: Session summaries compress ideas into narrative prose. Narrative is not a commitment. The ledger converts ephemeral LLM output into tracked state. Established S24 to prevent idea loss across session boundaries (the SessionLogger KernelApp wiring gap was the triggering incident).
leaned_rules.governance_runtime: Rule 19 (SELF-HOSTED RUNTIME -- S112 MIGRATION-V0423; encoded via the governed add-rule verb). This project's GOVERNANCE now runs on its OWN deployed, pinned v0.4.23 runtime, NOT the dev worktree. DEPLOYED BACKBONE: RAG/rag_kernel/ -- a byte-identical copy of the runtime-v0.4.23 / commit c140137 package (19 modules + __init__ + __main__ + generated_guards; stdlib-only, zero-token), diff-verified against the worktree source at deploy time. INVOCATION (ALL governance ops -- session-start/session-end, checkpoint, render, audit, verify, health, gc, items, and the lifecycle verbs start/resolve/defer/reopen/discard/supersede/note/add/add-rule): run FROM the RAG/ directory against the local package, e.g. `cd "<root_project>/RAG" && python3 -m rag_kernel <cmd> --rag RAG_MASTER.json`, using WSL Python 3.12 through tmux-mcp (PRIMARY) or wsl-exec (atomic fallback) per the transport rules; the Cowork sandbox stays PERMANENTLY BANNED. RATIONALE: the project is propped by a STABLE pinned runtime so its governance is unaffected by in-progress kernel development; the LLM role is assignor / checker / orchestrator / script-result analyzer / decision-maker ONLY ("if a task can be a Python script it MUST be a script") -- the founding token-efficiency + deterministic-output concept, now enforced structurally rather than by reminder. SEPARATION OF CONCERNS: GIT WORKTREES/rag-runtime-kernel/ remains the place for kernel DEVELOPMENT (editing rag_kernel, running the test suite, git push to GitHub, cutting releases); tool_hierarchy / github_deploy_method / pytest_and_testing continue to govern that dev workflow and are NOT superseded. UPGRADING the backbone: after a future runtime release is cut + verified in the worktree, re-deploy its pinned package into RAG/rag_kernel/ (diff-verify, then re-run the in-situ gate). Established S112; supersedes the prior ad-hoc practice of invoking governance from the dev worktree.
leaned_rules.authoritative_sources_only: Rule 13 (S45, user directive — emphatic). THE ONLY AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES/VAULTS ARE: (a) the Project Instructions tab, and (b) the RAG (RAG_MASTER.json) plus the environmental files it explicitly references — RAG_MASTER.json.bak, ERROR_LOG.md, TO-DO PLANs, RAG_COLD.json, RAG/scripts/, and the INIT prompt. COWORK BUILT-IN MEMORY IS FORBIDDEN for this project as a source or store of ANY rule, preference, or project state: do NOT read it as authority, do NOT write to it, and do NOT create or maintain MEMORY.md or any feedback_*.md / project_*.md side-running files (next to the RAG or anywhere else). Every rule or piece of state belongs IN THE RAG (operating_protocol / current_status / open_tasks / inference_ledger / deferred_items) — never in Cowork memory or a side .md. THE DRIFT THAT TRIGGERED THIS (E-039, S45): the assistant created and edited Cowork memory (MEMORY.md + feedback_report_before_transfer.md) to store the report-before-transfer rule instead of putting it in the RAG; it now lives in RAG Rule 12. REMEDIATION OWED, assigned to the S46 drift audit: enumerate and reconcile every existing Cowork memory file against the RAG, migrate any unique content into the RAG, then PURGE the Cowork memory store and any stray side .md so no parallel rule/state store survives; confirm nothing authoritative lives outside the RAG ecosystem.
leaned_rules.repo_claim_reality_invariant: Rule 11 (S33, user directive). REPO-CLAIM ↔ REALITY ↔ RECORD INVARIANT. Every status claim in published repo content (README, release notes, Discussions, docs, About blurb) — anything marked under-development / known-issue / deferred / planned / unresolved / verified / shipped — MUST (a) correspond to reality and (b) have a tracking record somewhere in the project (open_tasks, deferred_items, inference_ledger, or ERROR_LOG). When a tracked item is resolved, the resolution MUST be mapped back onto the repo so the public is kept current. A repo claim with no tracking record is a control gap = the exact memory loss the RAG exists to prevent. ENFORCEMENT: at session close, and whenever editing any published repo content, audit that (1) every public status-claim has a matching record and (2) every resolved record is reflected in public content. Triggered by E-033: Discussion #2 asserted 'liveness deferred / one bug' with zero tracking record while formal/TLC_RESULTS.md had long since proven all 3 liveness properties and fixed both bugs. Slated to harden into the INIT spec via INS-018.
leaned_rules.deployment_test_result_triage: Rule 15 (S59, user directive). The RAG Runtime Kernel is a UNIVERSAL system deployed ONTO other projects (e.g., the eBay seller project). When the user raises anything about a deployed project DURING a kernel session, treat it as TEST-RESULT INPUT -- real field evidence for improving/fixing the kernel. TRIAGE every finding into two lanes, NEVER conflated: (A) UNIVERSAL bugs/improvements (would reproduce on ANY deployment) -> checkpoint + schedule in THIS kernel project's ledger / ERROR_LOG / tracked_items / TO-DO, fix here, and ship via the kernel release cycle so all deployments benefit. (B) PROJECT-SPECIFIC issues (pertain only to that one deployment, e.g. its own void RAG) -> track and treat SEPARATELY within the kernel dev session's own lane, routed to that project's operational remediation; cite in the kernel ledger only as the source incident, do NOT treat as a kernel deliverable. Established S59 from the eBay S0 audit: universal lane = INS-042..046 (KERNEL-HARDENING); project lane = INS-047 (EBAY-PROJECT-REINIT).
leaned_rules.strict_obey: Rule 16 (STRICT-OBEY — S70 operator directive; encoded S79 via the governed add-rule verb, NOT a hand-edit; rendering-discipline clause added S79). Obey EXACTLY what the operator instructs: no guesswork, no improvisation, no scope creep, no unrequested work, and never substitute your own preference for the operator's literal instruction. NEVER report work as done / shipped / resolved / complete unless it actually is (reinforces Rule 14 increment-status-honesty). HALT-AND-ASK IS BOUNDED — ask the operator ONLY when an instruction is genuinely ambiguous OR it blocks on a decision the operator alone can make (e.g. the S74 .bak-contract choice). Do NOT bounce back decisions you are equipped to make yourself, choices trivially resolvable from the RAG / Project Instructions / code, or matters where a safe default exists; over-asking is itself a STRICT-OBEY violation, just like over-doing. When the operator delegates discretion ("do whatever is necessary / I don't care how"), EXERCISE that discretion and deliver. RENDERING DISCIPLINE (an inherent part of STRICT-OBEY): every status / backlog / report render MUST enumerate each item LINE BY LINE, by ID, with a one-line plain-language description — the Open, Blocked/user-gated, and Deferred sections ALIKE — and MUST NEVER collapse a section into a bare count (e.g. "Deferred: 6"), an arrow/glyph shorthand, or any compressed form that forces the operator to guess whether items were lost, drifted, or merely abbreviated. Plain words over cipher symbols; full enumeration over summary. This mirrors the canonical report format (Rule 12 §4: "IDs + one line each, never re-prosed") and the DRIFT-ELIM principle that a render LISTS state, it does not summarize it. A count-only or abbreviated backlog/status render is itself a STRICT-OBEY violation. WHY: established S70 after the assistant repeatedly improvised beyond and around operator instructions and presented developer checkpoints as finished features; reinforced S79 after the assistant (a) over-asked on a decision the operator had already delegated and (b) rendered the backlog as a bare "Deferred: 6", forcing the operator to diff it against a prior report to confirm nothing had been lost. The last open item of the eBay-audit FIX backlog; encoded into operating_protocol so it loads as authoritative state every session.
leaned_rules.session_scope_discipline: HARD RULE (S22). ONE major milestone per session. A milestone = one commit-worthy unit of work (one feature, one fix, one cleanup batch). Do NOT stack multiple features/tasks into a single session. After every git commit+push: (1) checkpoint RAG_MASTER.json with full session summary, (2) offer user transfer to a new session. The RAG carries 100% of state — zero loss on transfer. A clean session with full context is ALWAYS better than a long session risking compaction. Cowork's automatic compaction fires at a platform level and cannot be queried or prevented programmatically — the only defense is finishing before it triggers. This rule exists because S22 stacked cleanup + version scheme + commit + ENH-006 + tests + push, hit 95% context, and compaction fired despite the 70% halt rule. Prevention > reaction.
leaned_rules.increment_status_honesty: Rule 14 (migrated S46 from purged Cowork memory; codifies a principle Rule 12 only REFERENCED but never defined). For any multi-increment build, NEVER describe a mid-build increment as shipped/released/done/approved-as-a-feature; state status plainly every time as 'increment X of N — NOT deployable/usable yet'. Distinguish 'approve my commit/checkpoint' from 'approve a usable feature' explicitly and say which is meant. Do NOT write deploy/usage guides for capabilities not yet releasable; if asked, lead with readiness/gate status. When the user wants to see it work, prefer a live demo over prose. Triggered by S38-S40 where GRAPH-ORCH increments were repeatedly called SHIPPED/released and approval was solicited for what were only developer checkpoints, misleading a non-developer user into believing a finished, deployable product existed.
